quotes.material: The right metatarsus of FMNH PR 2081 (Figs. 99 - 104) is virtually complete, lacking only the metatarsal for digit I. All phalanges for the second and third digits are present, and only the distalmost two phalanges are missing from the fourth (Figs. 105 - 108). An isolated claw is all that remains of the first digit.
quotes.hallux: Immediately distal to this is a much larger teardrop-shaped feature ... This marks the attachment surface for MT I. Although MT I attached to the rest of the metatarsus posteriorly, the distal trochlea on MT I was oriented such that digit I was not reversed. [on the posteromedial surface of MT II]
quotes.digit_I_ungual: The ungual of digit I is much narrower than those of digits II and III, with an oval cross section and stronger ventral curvature in lateral view.
quotes.unguals_II_III: The unguals of digits II and III are triangular in cross-section, with broad, flattened ventral surfaces.
quotes.phalanges: The nonungual phalanges on each digit (Figs. 105 - 108) are progressively shorter distally.
quotes.mt_divergence: the shaft of MT IV diverges further laterally than its counterpart does medially; as a result, the distal condyle of MT III is closer to that of MT II than MT IV. This is reflected in footprints attributed to Tyrannosauridae (Lockley and Hunt, 1994), in which the cleft between the second and third digits lies anterior to that for the third and fourth.

boeye2026.cite: Boeye, Atkins-Weltman, King & Swann 2026, R. Soc. Open Sci. 13:252139, doi:10.1098/rsos.252139 (CC BY 4.0)
boeye2026.copy: dl/boeye2026/boeye.pdf (publisher PDF mirrored at dinodata.de; publisher site returned a bot challenge); text boeye.txt
boeye2026.depth_quote: In some well-preserved trackways of tyrannosaurs [34,36], digits III and IV appear to have a greater depth than impressions left by digit II, creating two distinct depressions in areas around the proximal pedal phalanges, with one centred on digits II and III and a second on digit IV [31,34-36].
boeye2026.strike_quote: a 'distal-first' foot-strike pattern where flesh of the foot ventral to the distal pedal phalanges make initial contact with the ground

mccrea2014_text.fl_proxy: Digit III length is calculated by summing the lengths of the pedal phalanges and adding 5% to the total ... the osteologic FL of digit III ... as a proxy for ichnologic FL

hip_height_m._locator: Discussion: 'Taking into account a flexion of the knee of 110 deg and a flexion at the ankle of 140 deg [65],[66], an estimated hip height of 2.30 m is obtained'

mccrea2014_text.diagnosis: Total divarication is variable, but is generally no greater than 80o. Divarication between digits III and IV is normally greater than between digits II and III. Metatarsal pad impression present with a wide caudal margin.

lallensack2022.cite: Lallensack, Farlow & Falkingham 2022, Palaeontology (author PDF https://researchonline.ljmu.ac.uk/15899/)
lallensack2022.quote_mtp_pads: The metatarsophalangeal pads of digits II and III seem to have been typically held clear of the ground by non-avian theropods, but may occasionally leave an impression (Thulborn 1990). The metatarsophalangeal pad of digit IV, on the other hand, is thought to have commonly been impressed (Farlow et al. 2000).
lallensack2022.quote_resting: the metatarso-phalangeal pad of digit IV is lying nearly along the axis of digit III instead of being located laterally as in walking trackways (Olsen & Rainforth 2003)

hutchinson2011.cite: Hutchinson et al. 2011, PLoS ONE 6:e26037, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0026037
hutchinson2011.text_plausible_com: the range of ~30-45% femur length for most minimal and maximal (also most dorsal and ventral) models; albeit with Sue at 44-61%; would cover our qualitative assessment of the most plausible COM range for adult Tyrannosaurus
hutchinson2011.text_ventral_com: Expressed as % femur length ventral to the hip, the COM was estimated to be 22-35% for the Carnegie and MOR specimens, a surprisingly conservative but otherwise similar 26-28% for Sue, 38-50% for Stan, and 35-54% for Jane.
hutchinson2011.table10_footnote: 'Mlimbs / Mbody' shows the percentage of body mass that the sampled limb mass (for left and right limbs) constitutes ... Tyrannosaurus ... 35-65 [upper-end (over)estimates]
hutchinson2011.segment_text: foot segment represents the distal tarsals (when present), metatarsus and all preserved digits
